ApprovalDecidedSignal.description: Parent to child: the decision the parked agent is waiting for.
ApprovalDecidedSignal.title: ApprovalDecidedSignal

AttemptFinishedSignal.description: Child AttemptWorkflow to parent, sent to the workflow id without a run id.
AttemptFinishedSignal.title: AttemptFinishedSignal

AttemptResumedPayload.description:
A Temporal retry inside the same attempt, e.g. after a worker crash, or an activity that carries on after an approval or
an answer. The worker emits it (entity.version 0), so the entity version cannot order it against the workflow's events of
the attempt. The rule for a consumer: events of one attempt are ordered by (`activity_attempt`, `state_version`), and
against the workflow's events by `occurred_at`; a resumed event never changes the attempt's status by itself, it only
says the attempt is running again.
AttemptResumedPayload.title: AttemptResumedPayload

Budget.description:
Limits. A missing field means no limit at this level.

Money is in micro-dollars so both languages keep it exact.
Budget.title: Budget

CompleteNodeInput.description:
Update ``completeNode``: a person completes a node by hand (04 §4). Allowed while the task is paused or taken over,
for a node that is not frozen and has no attempt running. It is not verified: the person is the verdict.
CompleteNodeInput.title: CompleteNodeInput

CompletionProposal.description: Update ``proposeCompletion``. Completion is a claim until verified (04 §5).
CompletionProposal.title: CompletionProposal

ConnectorSnapshot.description:
An MCP connector as the worker connects to it (15 M8): names and launch targets, never secret values.
Control resolves the tenant's connector to this when the configuration is set, so a running task keeps the
connector it was given even if the tenant's list changes.
ConnectorSnapshot.title: ConnectorSnapshot

DeclareBlockedOp.description: An agent says its own node cannot proceed (05 §2, agent rights).
DeclareBlockedOp.title: DeclareBlockedOp

EntityRef.description: Consumers keep, per entity, only the highest version they have seen (09 §1).
EntityRef.title: EntityRef

PermissionRuleSpec.description:
A permission rule a person allowed for the rest of a task: this tool, and what it is called with (a command
prefix for Bash, a path pattern for Write). It is what AgentScope suggests with the approval.
PermissionRuleSpec.title: PermissionRuleSpec

PlanArchive.description:
What was compacted out of the live plan: completed, frozen nodes nothing unfinished depends on. The nodes
themselves stay in the projection; this is the summary that keeps the plan's history explainable (04 §7).
PlanArchive.title: PlanArchive

PlanChangeCommand.description: Update ``submitPlanChange``. The whole command applies or none of it does.
PlanChangeCommand.title: PlanChangeCommand

PlanChangeRejected.description: No full graph here: Update results land in history (04 §4.1).
PlanChangeRejected.title: PlanChangeRejected

PlanReviewLimitReachedPayload.description:
The leader's reviews reached `Policy.max_review_rounds` (05 §7): the tasks created in the last round are done and
nobody reviewed them. The task asks for a review of its own (`task.status_changed`).
PlanReviewLimitReachedPayload.title: PlanReviewLimitReachedPayload

PlanView.description: Query ``getPlan``: the graph as the asking actor may see it.
PlanView.title: PlanView

Policy.description:
What an attempt may do (05 §6). Every layer (tenant, task, profile) can carry one; layers only tighten each
other: `denied_tools` add up and the smallest `exploration_max_tool_calls` wins. A missing field limits nothing.
Policy.title: Policy

SendMessageInput.description: Update ``sendMessage``; ``client_message_id`` doubles as the command id.
SendMessageInput.title: SendMessageInput

SopDefinition.description: What control stores for `sop_id@version`, and what the workflow compiles.
SopDefinition.title: SopDefinition

SopStepInfo.description:
Which part of a compiled SOP a node is (the plan keeps no other trace of the SOP): `role` `sop` is the `sop_stage`
node itself, `step` one step's agent node, `approval_before` and `approval_after` the approval nodes of a step with
`human_approval`. `index` (1-based) and `total` count the steps: "SOP X: step i/n".
SopStepInfo.title: SopStepInfo

SopVerifier.description:
Who judges a step and by what: extra criteria on top of the step's own description. A verifier is an independent
agent session of its own: it does not see how the executor worked, only the result.
SopVerifier.title: SopVerifier

TaskConfig.description:
What a task runs with, beside its goal (15 M8). `expert` replaces the task's profile for nodes that do not
name their own; `skills` and `connectors` are the complete sets to use, and None means the expert's defaults.
A change takes effect from the next attempt, never in the one that is running (11 §3).
TaskConfig.title: TaskConfig

TaskConfigChangedPayload.description: What the task runs with from its next attempt on. Connector ids only: the launch targets stay out of events.
TaskConfigChangedPayload.title: TaskConfigChangedPayload

Team.description:
A leader and members. The leader's expert plans the task; a node the leader gives to a role runs as that member's
expert, and one it gives to nobody runs as the leader. Teams do not nest (07 §1: depth 1).
Team.title: Team

TeamMember.description: One member of a team (15 M8, T8.6): a role the leader can give work to, and the expert who does it.
TeamMember.title: TeamMember

TeamMessagePayload.description:
One utterance in the team's group conversation, whatever made it (07 §5): the leader assigning work (`assign`), a member
answering (`reply`), a note posted for the team (`note`), the leader's review or final answer (`review`), the user (`user`) or
the runtime explaining a refusal (`system`). `to_roles` is who it is addressed to (mentions); empty is the whole group. A stage
emits them with entity {team, attempt_id}; plan-level ones (a TaskCreate given to a member, its result, a user message to a
member) have no stage: `attempt_id` is the attempt that made it (None for the user) and `round` is 0.
`role` and `label` repeat `from_role` and `from_label` (kept for consumers of the first shape of this event).
TeamMessagePayload.title: TeamMessagePayload

TeamRoundStartedPayload.description:
The leader of a team stage starts its `round`-th turn (07 §5). Team events carry the stage's attempt as their entity:
{kind: team, id: attempt_id}, with a version of their own.
TeamRoundStartedPayload.title: TeamRoundStartedPayload

TeamStageInfo.description:
What a view of a `team_stage` node says about its stage: the limits it runs under (from its spec, so nobody assumes the
defaults). The counters ({round, messages}) are on the stage's `team.*` events (`team.round_started` and `team.round_finished`).
TeamStageInfo.title: TeamStageInfo

TeamStageLimits.description: What bounds one team stage (07 §4). Whichever is reached first ends the stage with a reason, never silently.
TeamStageLimits.title: TeamStageLimits

TeamStageMember.description: One member of a team stage: the role the leader assigns work to, and the profile (an expert) that does it.
TeamStageMember.title: TeamStageMember

TeamStageSpec.description:
A bounded team inside one attempt (07): a leader and its members work on `goal` together. The leader runs as the
`leader` member's executor and hands work to the others; what it finishes with is the stage's result. `workspace_access`
is what the members get of the task workspace: a copy of its latest snapshot that is thrown away (`read`), or nothing
(`none`). Only the leader writes the task's workspace (the node's own `workspace_access`).
TeamStageSpec.title: TeamStageSpec

UpdateTaskConfigInput.description:
Replaces the task's configuration. `base_config_version` is the version the caller read; a newer one in
place means the caller decided on stale data and gets CONFIG_VERSION_CONFLICT.
UpdateTaskConfigInput.title: UpdateTaskConfigInput

AskUserQuestion.description:
One structured question of `ask_user`: a short chip label, the question and 0-4 options. The user can always type
their own answer, so there is no "other" option.
AskUserQuestion.title: AskUserQuestion
